name: Expense Policy Check: Ladder
description: Ten frozen levels of expense auditing for one team, against a written policy with exceptions to the exceptions: every line paid less than claimed (rule and amount), what to pay each person, and the reclaimable VAT. Levels 1-2 are one monthly batch with two and four rules; from level 3 a level is two to six consecutive monthly batches for the same people, and the months depend on each other: mileage at 45p then 25p after 10,000 miles is counted through the months and restarts on 6 April, expenses come back as duplicates in later months, late lines need an approval for their own claim, meal limits are shared with earlier lines of the same day, and (from level 5) cash advances are set off month by month and carried on. The answer carries the state: each month's payout per person, the advances left and the miles to date, so one early slip moves every later month. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.
hook: Six months of expense claims for one team, every month depending on the last. How far up can it pay everyone right?
author: Gauntlet Core

cases.prompt:
I run the monthly expenses check. Please audit this batch of claim lines against our policy and tell me what to pay.

Expenses policy (Finance, version 8) — apply every rule exactly as written.

A. Rules, in this order. A line breaks a rule when that rule reduces what the company pays for it.
 1. NO_RECEIPT — any line of £25.00 or more without a receipt pays £0.
 2. HOTEL_CAP — hotels are paid up to a limit per night: London £180, other UK cities £120.
B. Report a line as non-compliant when it is paid less than its claimed amount (in pounds). Give the FIRST rule in the list above that reduced it, and the amount to pay. Lines paid in full (or more) are compliant and must not be listed.
C. VAT. The company reclaims the VAT shown on a line only if the line is paid in full and has a receipt.

Claim C-3446 — Yasmin Demir (Operations), submitted Mon 28 Sep 2026.
  L01 | Fri 4 Sep 2026 | Central Stay Manchester, Manchester | Hotel, 2 nights | £171.14 | VAT £28.52 | receipt attached
  L02 | Fri 4 Sep 2026 | National Rail (LNER/Avanti/GWR) | Rail London Euston – Manchester Piccadilly return, standard class | £92.40 | receipt attached
  L03 | Mon 7 Sep 2026 | High Street Pharmacy | First-aid kit restock | £24.99 | no receipt
  L04 | Thu 24 Sep 2026 | Royal Mail | Special Delivery postage | £8.23 | receipt attached

Claim C-3106 — Lachlan Nwosu (Finance), submitted Mon 28 Sep 2026.
  L05 | Tue 1 Sep 2026 | Wharfside Hotel Leeds, Leeds | Hotel, 2 nights | £317.30 | VAT £52.88 | receipt attached
  L06 | Tue 1 Sep 2026 | National Rail (LNER/Avanti/GWR) | Rail London King's Cross – Leeds return, standard class | £86.70 | receipt attached
  L07 | Fri 4 Sep 2026 | City Car Parks | Parking, client visit | £32.02 | VAT £5.34 | receipt attached
  L08 | Mon 21 Sep 2026 | Royal Mail | Special Delivery postage | £25.00 | no receipt

Answer with one JSON object in exactly this shape:
{"non_compliant": {"L03": {"rule": "HOTEL_CAP", "pay": 360.00}, "L07": {"rule": "NO_RECEIPT", "pay": 0}, ...}, "paid_out": {"September 2026": {"Full Name": 512.40, ...}}, "vat_reclaimable": 41.27}
- non_compliant: one entry per line that is paid less than claimed, keyed by line number, with the rule (one of NO_RECEIPT, HOTEL_CAP) and the amount to pay in pounds. Do not list lines that are paid in full.
- paid_out: for each month (keyed by the month as written above), the amount to pay each employee (every employee) for that month's batch.
- vat_reclaimable: the total VAT the company can reclaim.
All amounts in pounds to the penny (a £ sign and thousands separators are fine). Marking: each listed line has two fields (rule, amount); every payout, advance, miles figure and the VAT is a field. Routine fields are worth 1 point; fields that need extra care (the £25.00 edge, the VAT) are worth 3, and every payout is worth 3 (together about a third of the points). Every line you list that should not be listed costs two fields at 3 points each. Reply with the JSON object only (a ```json code block is fine); key order, spacing and letter case do not matter. Give one value per field: a field with two values is marked wrong, and if you give more than one JSON answer only the last one counts.
cases.notes: [level 1] 1 month, 8 claim lines from 2 employees in 2 claims. Rules in play: 2 families (receipt, hotel); 2 lines paid less than claimed. Key = audit() of verification/realworld-work/expenses.py over every month's lines in order, exact decimals; second derivations: month-by-month audits over the months so far give every line the same result, the advance set-off step by step equals its closed form, miles summed directly. Trap fields 3 points, routine 1, each payout / advance / miles figure 3. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly bigger than the one below and stacking more rule families of the same policy. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.

cases.prompt:
I've been off, so the expenses for March 2026 to April 2026 were never checked or paid. Please audit every monthly batch against our policy, in order, and tell me what to pay each person each month.

Expenses policy (Finance, version 8) — apply every rule exactly as written.

A. Conversion. Amounts in euros or US dollars are converted to pounds at the rate in the rate table, rounded to the nearest penny, BEFORE any limit is applied. All limits are in pounds.
B. Months. The batches below are processed month by month, in order, and the line numbers run on through the months. Every rule that looks at other lines (duplicates, meal limits, mileage) also looks at the lines of earlier months.
C. Rules, in this order. A line breaks a rule when that rule reduces what the company pays for it.
 1. LATE — a line whose expense date is more than 60 days before its claim's submission date pays £0, unless the register holds a late-submission approval (type LATE) for that claim number.
 2. DUPLICATE — the same expense claimed again (same employee, date, merchant and amount, in the same or another claim, in any month): the later line (higher line number) pays £0.
 3. NO_RECEIPT — any line of £25.00 or more (after conversion) without a receipt pays £0. Mileage needs no receipt.
 4. ALCOHOL — alcohol is never paid (deduct the alcohol amount shown on the line, converted if needed), except on client entertainment approved under rule 7, where alcohol is paid up to £15 per head (heads counted as in rule 7) and only the excess is deducted.
 5. MEAL_CAP — meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) are paid up to a limit for each employee, each city and each day: London £40, other UK cities £30, Paris £48, Dublin £44, New York £60. Meals in different cities on the same day are capped separately, each against its own city's limit. When one employee has several meals in the same city on the same day, take them in line order: each is paid up to what is left of that limit (after any alcohol deduction).
 6. HOTEL_CAP — hotels are paid up to a limit per night: London £180, other UK cities £120, Paris £190, Dublin £170, New York £240.
 7. ENTERTAINMENT_CAP — client entertainment is paid up to £60 per head (count everyone at the table, staff included), after any alcohol deduction. It is approved only if the line's approval reference is in the register as type ENT for the same employee; an approval mentioned on a claim but missing from the register, or registered for someone else, does not count. Approved entertainment is paid in full (alcohol as in rule 4); if the register gives a limit, the amount left after any alcohol deduction is capped at that limit.
 8. RAIL_CLASS — rail travel is paid at standard class: a first-class ticket is paid at the standard fare shown on the line.
 9. MILEAGE_RATE — business mileage in a private car is paid at 45p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year and 25p a mile after that, plus 5p a mile for each colleague carried as a passenger (the passenger supplement does not count towards the 10,000). The tax year runs 6 April to 5 April. Count each employee's miles in date order across all their claims in all the months below, starting from the miles paid before the first month in the tax year named on their first claim (in any other tax year, start from 0); a journey that crosses 10,000 is split. Mileage is paid at the correct rate whatever amount was claimed.
D. Report a line as non-compliant when it is paid less than its claimed amount (in pounds). Give the FIRST rule in the list above that reduced it, and the amount to pay. Lines paid in full (or more) are compliant and must not be listed; a mileage line claimed below the correct amount is paid the correct amount and is compliant.
E. VAT. The company reclaims the VAT shown on a line only if the line is paid in full, is in pounds (a UK expense), has a receipt and is not client entertainment. Mileage carries no VAT.

Rate table (all the months below): €1 = £0.87, $1 = £0.78.

Rules in play: 11 families (receipt, hotel, meal, rail, alcohol, late, duplicate, months, entertainment, mileage, conversion); 44 lines paid less than claimed. Key = audit() of verification/realworld-work/expenses.py over every month's lines in order, exact decimals; second derivations: month-by-month audits over the months so far give every line the same result, the advance set-off step by step equals its closed form, miles summed directly. Trap fields 3 points, routine 1, each payout / advance / miles figure 7. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly bigger than the one below and stacking more rule families of the same policy. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.

cases.prompt:
I've been off, so the expenses for February 2026 to April 2026 were never checked or paid. Please audit every monthly batch against our policy, in order, and tell me what to pay each person each month.

Expenses policy (Finance, version 8) — apply every rule exactly as written.

A. Conversion. Amounts in euros or US dollars are converted to pounds at the rate in the rate table, rounded to the nearest penny, BEFORE any limit is applied. All limits are in pounds.
B. Months. The batches below are processed month by month, in order, and the line numbers run on through the months. Every rule that looks at other lines (duplicates, meal limits, mileage) also looks at the lines of earlier months.
C. Rules, in this order. A line breaks a rule when that rule reduces what the company pays for it.
 1. LATE — a line whose expense date is more than 60 days before its claim's submission date pays £0, unless the register holds a late-submission approval (type LATE) for that claim number.
 2. DUPLICATE — the same expense claimed again (same employee, date, merchant and amount, in the same or another claim, in any month): the later line (higher line number) pays £0.
 3. NO_RECEIPT — any line of £25.00 or more (after conversion) without a receipt pays £0. Mileage needs no receipt.
 4. ALCOHOL — alcohol is never paid (deduct the alcohol amount shown on the line, converted if needed), except on client entertainment approved under rule 7, where alcohol is paid up to £15 per head (heads counted as in rule 7) and only the excess is deducted.
 5. MEAL_CAP — meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) are paid up to a limit for each employee, each city and each day: London £40, other UK cities £30, Paris £48, Dublin £44, New York £60. Meals in different cities on the same day are capped separately, each against its own city's limit. A city's limit is £20 higher on a day when the same employee has a hotel stay in that city in these batches covering the night of that day (a hotel line dated D for N nights covers the nights of D to D+N-1, not the morning of departure). When one employee has several meals in the same city on the same day, take them in line order: each is paid up to what is left of that limit (after any alcohol deduction).
 6. HOTEL_CAP — hotels are paid up to a limit per night: London £180, other UK cities £120, Paris £190, Dublin £170, New York £240.
 7. ENTERTAINMENT_CAP — client entertainment is paid up to £60 per head (count everyone at the table, staff included), after any alcohol deduction. It is approved only if the line's approval reference is in the register as type ENT for the same employee; an approval mentioned on a claim but missing from the register, or registered for someone else, does not count. Approved entertainment is paid in full (alcohol as in rule 4); if the register gives a limit, the amount left after any alcohol deduction is capped at that limit.
 8. RAIL_CLASS — rail travel is paid at standard class: a first-class ticket is paid at the standard fare shown on the line.
 9. MILEAGE_RATE — business mileage in a private car is paid at 45p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year and 25p a mile after that, plus 5p a mile for each colleague carried as a passenger (the passenger supplement does not count towards the 10,000). The tax year runs 6 April to 5 April. Count each employee's miles in date order across all their claims in all the months below, starting from the miles paid before the first month in the tax year named on their first claim (in any other tax year, start from 0); a journey that crosses 10,000 is split. Mileage is paid at the correct rate whatever amount was claimed.
D. Report a line as non-compliant when it is paid less than its claimed amount (in pounds). Give the FIRST rule in the list above that reduced it, and the amount to pay. Lines paid in full (or more) are compliant and must not be listed; a mileage line claimed below the correct amount is paid the correct amount and is compliant.
E. VAT. The company reclaims the VAT shown on a line only if the line is paid in full, is in pounds (a UK expense), has a receipt and is not client entertainment. Mileage carries no VAT.
F. Cash advances. An advance still outstanding is set off against what the employee is owed, month by month: the payout for a month is what that month's lines pay the employee minus the advance outstanding (never below zero), and whatever the set-off does not use stays outstanding for the next month. An advance paid during a month is outstanding only from the next month on.

cases.prompt:
I've been off, so the expenses for February 2026 to April 2026 were never checked or paid. Please audit every monthly batch against our policy, in order, and tell me what to pay each person each month.

Expenses policy (Finance, version 8) — apply every rule exactly as written.

A. Conversion. Amounts in euros or US dollars are converted to pounds at the rate in the rate table, rounded to the nearest penny, BEFORE any limit is applied. All limits are in pounds.
B. Months. The batches below are processed month by month, in order, and the line numbers run on through the months. Every rule that looks at other lines (duplicates, meal limits, mileage) also looks at the lines of earlier months.
C. Rules, in this order. A line breaks a rule when that rule reduces what the company pays for it.
 1. LATE — a line whose expense date is more than 60 days before its claim's submission date pays £0, unless the register holds a late-submission approval (type LATE) for that claim number.
 2. DUPLICATE — the same expense claimed again (same employee, date, merchant and amount, in the same or another claim, in any month): the later line (higher line number) pays £0.
 3. NO_RECEIPT — any line of £25.00 or more (after conversion) without a receipt pays £0. Mileage needs no receipt.
 4. ALCOHOL — alcohol is never paid (deduct the alcohol amount shown on the line, converted if needed), except on client entertainment approved under rule 7, where alcohol is paid up to £15 per head (heads counted as in rule 7) and only the excess is deducted.
 5. MEAL_CAP — meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) are paid up to a limit for each employee, each city and each day: London £40, other UK cities £30, Paris £48, Dublin £44, New York £60. Meals in different cities on the same day are capped separately, each against its own city's limit. A city's limit is £20 higher on a day when the same employee has a hotel stay in that city in these batches covering the night of that day (a hotel line dated D for N nights covers the nights of D to D+N-1, not the morning of departure). When one employee has several meals in the same city on the same day, take them in line order: each is paid up to what is left of that limit (after any alcohol deduction).
 6. HOTEL_CAP — hotels are paid up to a limit per night: London £180, other UK cities £120, Paris £190, Dublin £170, New York £240.
 7. ENTERTAINMENT_CAP — client entertainment is paid up to £60 per head (count everyone at the table, staff included), after any alcohol deduction. It is approved only if the line's approval reference is in the register as type ENT for the same employee; an approval mentioned on a claim but missing from the register, or registered for someone else, does not count. Approved entertainment is paid in full (alcohol as in rule 4); if the register gives a limit, the amount left after any alcohol deduction is capped at that limit.
 8. RAIL_CLASS — rail travel is paid at standard class: a first-class ticket is paid at the standard fare shown on the line.
 9. MILEAGE_RATE — business mileage in a private car is paid at 45p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year and 25p a mile after that, plus 5p a mile for each colleague carried as a passenger (the passenger supplement does not count towards the 10,000). The tax year runs 6 April to 5 April. Count each employee's miles in date order across all their claims in all the months below, starting from the miles paid before the first month in the tax year named on their first claim (in any other tax year, start from 0); a journey that crosses 10,000 is split. Mileage is paid at the correct rate whatever amount was claimed.
D. Report a line as non-compliant when it is paid less than its claimed amount (in pounds). Give the FIRST rule in the list above that reduced it, and the amount to pay. Lines paid in full (or more) are compliant and must not be listed; a mileage line claimed below the correct amount is paid the correct amount and is compliant.
E. VAT. The company reclaims the VAT shown on a line only if the line is paid in full, is in pounds (a UK expense), has a receipt and is not client entertainment. Mileage carries no VAT.
F. Cash advances. An advance still outstanding is set off against what the employee is owed, month by month: the payout for a month is what that month's lines pay the employee minus the advance outstanding (never below zero), and whatever the set-off does not use stays outstanding for the next month. An advance paid during a month is outstanding only from the next month on.

- advances_left: for every employee who has had an advance, the advance still outstanding after the April 2026 batch.
- miles_to_date: for every employee with a mileage line, their business miles in the tax year of April 2026 once the April 2026 batch is counted (the miles before the first month included when that is the same tax year).

Routine fields are worth 1 point; fields that need extra care (shared or uplifted meal limits, approvals and their limits, mileage thresholds and passengers, late or duplicate lines, the £25.00 edge, the VAT) are worth 3, and every payout, advance and miles figure is worth 9 (together about a third of the points). Every line you list that should not be listed costs two fields at 3 points each. Reply with the JSON object only (a ```json code block is fine); key order, spacing and letter case do not matter. Give one value per field: a field with two values is marked wrong, and if you give more than one JSON answer only the last one counts.
cases.notes: [level 6] 3 months, 304 claim lines from 5 employees in 21 claims. Rules in play: 13 families (receipt, hotel, meal, rail, alcohol, late, duplicate, months, entertainment, mileage, conversion, meal-uplift, advances); 115 lines paid less than claimed. Key = audit() of verification/realworld-work/expenses.py over every month's lines in order, exact decimals; second derivations: month-by-month audits over the months so far give every line the same result, the advance set-off step by step equals its closed form, miles summed directly. Trap fields 3 points, routine 1, each payout / advance / miles figure 9. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly bigger than the one below and stacking more rule families of the same policy. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.

cases.prompt:
I've been off, so the expenses for January 2026 to April 2026 were never checked or paid. Please audit every monthly batch against our policy, in order, and tell me what to pay each person each month.

Expenses policy (Finance, version 8) — apply every rule exactly as written.

A. Conversion. Amounts in euros or US dollars are converted to pounds at the rate in the rate table, rounded to the nearest penny, BEFORE any limit is applied. All limits are in pounds.
B. Months. The batches below are processed month by month, in order, and the line numbers run on through the months. Every rule that looks at other lines (duplicates, meal limits, mileage) also looks at the lines of earlier months.
C. Rules, in this order. A line breaks a rule when that rule reduces what the company pays for it.
 1. LATE — a line whose expense date is more than 60 days before its claim's submission date pays £0, unless the register holds a late-submission approval (type LATE) for that claim number.
 2. DUPLICATE — the same expense claimed again (same employee, date, merchant and amount, in the same or another claim, in any month): the later line (higher line number) pays £0.
 3. NO_RECEIPT — any line of £25.00 or more (after conversion) without a receipt pays £0. Mileage needs no receipt.
 4. ALCOHOL — alcohol is never paid (deduct the alcohol amount shown on the line, converted if needed), except on client entertainment approved under rule 7, where alcohol is paid up to £15 per head (heads counted as in rule 7) and only the excess is deducted.
 5. MEAL_CAP — meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) are paid up to a limit for each employee, each city and each day: London £40, other UK cities £30, Paris £48, Dublin £44, New York £60. Meals in different cities on the same day are capped separately, each against its own city's limit. A city's limit is £20 higher on a day when the same employee has a hotel stay in that city in these batches covering the night of that day (a hotel line dated D for N nights covers the nights of D to D+N-1, not the morning of departure). When one employee has several meals in the same city on the same day, take them in line order: each is paid up to what is left of that limit (after any alcohol deduction).
 6. HOTEL_CAP — hotels are paid up to a limit per night: London £180, other UK cities £120, Paris £190, Dublin £170, New York £240.
 7. ENTERTAINMENT_CAP — client entertainment is paid up to £60 per head (count everyone at the table, staff included), after any alcohol deduction. It is approved only if the line's approval reference is in the register as type ENT for the same employee; an approval mentioned on a claim but missing from the register, or registered for someone else, does not count. Approved entertainment is paid in full (alcohol as in rule 4); if the register gives a limit, the amount left after any alcohol deduction is capped at that limit.
 8. RAIL_CLASS — rail travel is paid at standard class: a first-class ticket is paid at the standard fare shown on the line.
 9. MILEAGE_RATE — business mileage in a private car is paid at 45p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year and 25p a mile after that, plus 5p a mile for each colleague carried as a passenger (the passenger supplement does not count towards the 10,000). The tax year runs 6 April to 5 April. Count each employee's miles in date order across all their claims in all the months below, starting from the miles paid before the first month in the tax year named on their first claim (in any other tax year, start from 0); a journey that crosses 10,000 is split. Mileage is paid at the correct rate whatever amount was claimed.
D. Report a line as non-compliant when it is paid less than its claimed amount (in pounds). Give the FIRST rule in the list above that reduced it, and the amount to pay. Lines paid in full (or more) are compliant and must not be listed; a mileage line claimed below the correct amount is paid the correct amount and is compliant.
E. VAT. The company reclaims the VAT shown on a line only if the line is paid in full, is in pounds (a UK expense), has a receipt and is not client entertainment. Mileage carries no VAT.
F. Cash advances. An advance still outstanding is set off against what the employee is owed, month by month: the payout for a month is what that month's lines pay the employee minus the advance outstanding (never below zero), and whatever the set-off does not use stays outstanding for the next month. An advance paid during a month is outstanding only from the next month on.

cases.prompt:
I've been off, so the expenses for January 2026 to April 2026 were never checked or paid. Please audit every monthly batch against our policy, in order, and tell me what to pay each person each month.

Expenses policy (Finance, version 8) — apply every rule exactly as written.

A. Conversion. Amounts in euros or US dollars are converted to pounds at the rate in the rate table, rounded to the nearest penny, BEFORE any limit is applied. All limits are in pounds.
B. Months. The batches below are processed month by month, in order, and the line numbers run on through the months. Every rule that looks at other lines (duplicates, meal limits, mileage) also looks at the lines of earlier months.
C. Rules, in this order. A line breaks a rule when that rule reduces what the company pays for it.
 1. LATE — a line whose expense date is more than 60 days before its claim's submission date pays £0, unless the register holds a late-submission approval (type LATE) for that claim number.
 2. DUPLICATE — the same expense claimed again (same employee, date, merchant and amount, in the same or another claim, in any month): the later line (higher line number) pays £0.
 3. NO_RECEIPT — any line of £25.00 or more (after conversion) without a receipt pays £0. Mileage needs no receipt.
 4. ALCOHOL — alcohol is never paid (deduct the alcohol amount shown on the line, converted if needed), except on client entertainment approved under rule 7, where alcohol is paid up to £15 per head (heads counted as in rule 7) and only the excess is deducted.
 5. MEAL_CAP — meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) are paid up to a limit for each employee, each city and each day: London £40, other UK cities £30, Paris £48, Dublin £44, New York £60. Meals in different cities on the same day are capped separately, each against its own city's limit. A city's limit is £20 higher on a day when the same employee has a hotel stay in that city in these batches covering the night of that day (a hotel line dated D for N nights covers the nights of D to D+N-1, not the morning of departure). When one employee has several meals in the same city on the same day, take them in line order: each is paid up to what is left of that limit (after any alcohol deduction).
 6. HOTEL_CAP — hotels are paid up to a limit per night: London £180, other UK cities £120, Paris £190, Dublin £170, New York £240.
 7. ENTERTAINMENT_CAP — client entertainment is paid up to £60 per head (count everyone at the table, staff included), after any alcohol deduction. It is approved only if the line's approval reference is in the register as type ENT for the same employee; an approval mentioned on a claim but missing from the register, or registered for someone else, does not count. Approved entertainment is paid in full (alcohol as in rule 4); if the register gives a limit, the amount left after any alcohol deduction is capped at that limit.
 8. RAIL_CLASS — rail travel is paid at standard class: a first-class ticket is paid at the standard fare shown on the line.
 9. MILEAGE_RATE — business mileage in a private car is paid at 45p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year and 25p a mile after that, plus 5p a mile for each colleague carried as a passenger (the passenger supplement does not count towards the 10,000). The tax year runs 6 April to 5 April. Count each employee's miles in date order across all their claims in all the months below, starting from the miles paid before the first month in the tax year named on their first claim (in any other tax year, start from 0); a journey that crosses 10,000 is split. Mileage is paid at the correct rate whatever amount was claimed.
D. Report a line as non-compliant when it is paid less than its claimed amount (in pounds). Give the FIRST rule in the list above that reduced it, and the amount to pay. Lines paid in full (or more) are compliant and must not be listed; a mileage line claimed below the correct amount is paid the correct amount and is compliant.
E. VAT. The company reclaims the VAT shown on a line only if the line is paid in full, is in pounds (a UK expense), has a receipt and is not client entertainment. Mileage carries no VAT.
F. Cash advances. An advance still outstanding is set off against what the employee is owed, month by month: the payout for a month is what that month's lines pay the employee minus the advance outstanding (never below zero), and whatever the set-off does not use stays outstanding for the next month. An advance paid during a month is outstanding only from the next month on.

- non_compliant: one entry per line that is paid less than claimed, keyed by line number, with the rule (one of LATE, DUPLICATE, NO_RECEIPT, ALCOHOL, MEAL_CAP, HOTEL_CAP, ENTERTAINMENT_CAP, RAIL_CLASS, MILEAGE_RATE) and the amount to pay in pounds. Do not list lines that are paid in full.

- advances_left: for every employee who has had an advance, the advance still outstanding after the April 2026 batch.
- miles_to_date: for every employee with a mileage line, their business miles in the tax year of April 2026 once the April 2026 batch is counted (the miles before the first month included when that is the same tax year).

All amounts in pounds to the penny (a £ sign and thousands separators are fine). Marking: each listed line has two fields (rule, amount); every payout, advance, miles figure and the VAT is a field. Routine fields are worth 1 point; fields that need extra care (shared or uplifted meal limits, approvals and their limits, mileage thresholds and passengers, late or duplicate lines, the £25.00 edge, the VAT) are worth 3, and every payout, advance and miles figure is worth 12 (together about a third of the points). Every line you list that should not be listed costs two fields at 3 points each. Reply with the JSON object only (a ```json code block is fine); key order, spacing and letter case do not matter. Give one value per field: a field with two values is marked wrong, and if you give more than one JSON answer only the last one counts.
cases.notes: [level 8] 4 months, 519 claim lines from 6 employees in 36 claims. Rules in play: 13 families (receipt, hotel, meal, rail, alcohol, late, duplicate, months, entertainment, mileage, conversion, meal-uplift, advances); 226 lines paid less than claimed. Key = audit() of verification/realworld-work/expenses.py over every month's lines in order, exact decimals; second derivations: month-by-month audits over the months so far give every line the same result, the advance set-off step by step equals its closed form, miles summed directly. Trap fields 3 points, routine 1, each payout / advance / miles figure 12. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly bigger than the one below and stacking more rule families of the same policy. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.

cases.prompt:
I've been off, so the expenses for December 2026 to April 2027 were never checked or paid. Please audit every monthly batch against our policy, in order, and tell me what to pay each person each month.

Expenses policy (Finance, version 8) — apply every rule exactly as written.

A. Conversion. Amounts in euros or US dollars are converted to pounds at the rate in the rate table, rounded to the nearest penny, BEFORE any limit is applied. All limits are in pounds.
B. Months. The batches below are processed month by month, in order, and the line numbers run on through the months. Every rule that looks at other lines (duplicates, meal limits, mileage) also looks at the lines of earlier months.
C. Rules, in this order. A line breaks a rule when that rule reduces what the company pays for it.
 1. LATE — a line whose expense date is more than 60 days before its claim's submission date pays £0, unless the register holds a late-submission approval (type LATE) for that claim number.
 2. DUPLICATE — the same expense claimed again (same employee, date, merchant and amount, in the same or another claim, in any month): the later line (higher line number) pays £0.
 3. NO_RECEIPT — any line of £25.00 or more (after conversion) without a receipt pays £0. Mileage needs no receipt.
 4. ALCOHOL — alcohol is never paid (deduct the alcohol amount shown on the line, converted if needed), except on client entertainment approved under rule 7, where alcohol is paid up to £15 per head (heads counted as in rule 7) and only the excess is deducted.
 5. MEAL_CAP — meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) are paid up to a limit for each employee, each city and each day: London £40, other UK cities £30, Paris £48, Dublin £44, New York £60. Meals in different cities on the same day are capped separately, each against its own city's limit. A city's limit is £20 higher on a day when the same employee has a hotel stay in that city in these batches covering the night of that day (a hotel line dated D for N nights covers the nights of D to D+N-1, not the morning of departure). When one employee has several meals in the same city on the same day, take them in line order: each is paid up to what is left of that limit (after any alcohol deduction).
 6. HOTEL_CAP — hotels are paid up to a limit per night: London £180, other UK cities £120, Paris £190, Dublin £170, New York £240.
 7. ENTERTAINMENT_CAP — client entertainment is paid up to £60 per head (count everyone at the table, staff included), after any alcohol deduction. It is approved only if the line's approval reference is in the register as type ENT for the same employee; an approval mentioned on a claim but missing from the register, or registered for someone else, does not count. Approved entertainment is paid in full (alcohol as in rule 4); if the register gives a limit, the amount left after any alcohol deduction is capped at that limit.
 8. RAIL_CLASS — rail travel is paid at standard class: a first-class ticket is paid at the standard fare shown on the line.
 9. MILEAGE_RATE — business mileage in a private car is paid at 45p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year and 25p a mile after that, plus 5p a mile for each colleague carried as a passenger (the passenger supplement does not count towards the 10,000). The tax year runs 6 April to 5 April. Count each employee's miles in date order across all their claims in all the months below, starting from the miles paid before the first month in the tax year named on their first claim (in any other tax year, start from 0); a journey that crosses 10,000 is split. Mileage is paid at the correct rate whatever amount was claimed.
D. Report a line as non-compliant when it is paid less than its claimed amount (in pounds). Give the FIRST rule in the list above that reduced it, and the amount to pay. Lines paid in full (or more) are compliant and must not be listed; a mileage line claimed below the correct amount is paid the correct amount and is compliant.
E. VAT. The company reclaims the VAT shown on a line only if the line is paid in full, is in pounds (a UK expense), has a receipt and is not client entertainment. Mileage carries no VAT.
F. Cash advances. An advance still outstanding is set off against what the employee is owed, month by month: the payout for a month is what that month's lines pay the employee minus the advance outstanding (never below zero), and whatever the set-off does not use stays outstanding for the next month. An advance paid during a month is outstanding only from the next month on.

cases.prompt:
I've been off, so the expenses for December 2026 to May 2027 were never checked or paid. Please audit every monthly batch against our policy, in order, and tell me what to pay each person each month.

Expenses policy (Finance, version 8) — apply every rule exactly as written.

A. Conversion. Amounts in euros or US dollars are converted to pounds at the rate in the rate table, rounded to the nearest penny, BEFORE any limit is applied. All limits are in pounds.
B. Months. The batches below are processed month by month, in order, and the line numbers run on through the months. Every rule that looks at other lines (duplicates, meal limits, mileage) also looks at the lines of earlier months.
C. Rules, in this order. A line breaks a rule when that rule reduces what the company pays for it.
 1. LATE — a line whose expense date is more than 60 days before its claim's submission date pays £0, unless the register holds a late-submission approval (type LATE) for that claim number.
 2. DUPLICATE — the same expense claimed again (same employee, date, merchant and amount, in the same or another claim, in any month): the later line (higher line number) pays £0.
 3. NO_RECEIPT — any line of £25.00 or more (after conversion) without a receipt pays £0. Mileage needs no receipt.
 4. ALCOHOL — alcohol is never paid (deduct the alcohol amount shown on the line, converted if needed), except on client entertainment approved under rule 7, where alcohol is paid up to £15 per head (heads counted as in rule 7) and only the excess is deducted.
 5. MEAL_CAP — meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) are paid up to a limit for each employee, each city and each day: London £40, other UK cities £30, Paris £48, Dublin £44, New York £60. Meals in different cities on the same day are capped separately, each against its own city's limit. A city's limit is £20 higher on a day when the same employee has a hotel stay in that city in these batches covering the night of that day (a hotel line dated D for N nights covers the nights of D to D+N-1, not the morning of departure). When one employee has several meals in the same city on the same day, take them in line order: each is paid up to what is left of that limit (after any alcohol deduction).
 6. HOTEL_CAP — hotels are paid up to a limit per night: London £180, other UK cities £120, Paris £190, Dublin £170, New York £240.
 7. ENTERTAINMENT_CAP — client entertainment is paid up to £60 per head (count everyone at the table, staff included), after any alcohol deduction. It is approved only if the line's approval reference is in the register as type ENT for the same employee; an approval mentioned on a claim but missing from the register, or registered for someone else, does not count. Approved entertainment is paid in full (alcohol as in rule 4); if the register gives a limit, the amount left after any alcohol deduction is capped at that limit.
 8. RAIL_CLASS — rail travel is paid at standard class: a first-class ticket is paid at the standard fare shown on the line.
 9. MILEAGE_RATE — business mileage in a private car is paid at 45p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year and 25p a mile after that, plus 5p a mile for each colleague carried as a passenger (the passenger supplement does not count towards the 10,000). The tax year runs 6 April to 5 April. Count each employee's miles in date order across all their claims in all the months below, starting from the miles paid before the first month in the tax year named on their first claim (in any other tax year, start from 0); a journey that crosses 10,000 is split. Mileage is paid at the correct rate whatever amount was claimed.
D. Report a line as non-compliant when it is paid less than its claimed amount (in pounds). Give the FIRST rule in the list above that reduced it, and the amount to pay. Lines paid in full (or more) are compliant and must not be listed; a mileage line claimed below the correct amount is paid the correct amount and is compliant.
E. VAT. The company reclaims the VAT shown on a line only if the line is paid in full, is in pounds (a UK expense), has a receipt and is not client entertainment. Mileage carries no VAT.
F. Cash advances. An advance still outstanding is set off against what the employee is owed, month by month: the payout for a month is what that month's lines pay the employee minus the advance outstanding (never below zero), and whatever the set-off does not use stays outstanding for the next month. An advance paid during a month is outstanding only from the next month on.

- paid_out: for each month (keyed by the month as written above), the amount to pay each employee (every employee) for that month's batch, after setting off any advance.
- advances_left: for every employee who has had an advance, the advance still outstanding after the May 2027 batch.
- miles_to_date: for every employee with a mileage line, their business miles in the tax year of May 2027 once the May 2027 batch is counted (the miles before the first month included when that is the same tax year).
- vat_reclaimable: the total VAT the company can reclaim over all the months.
All amounts in pounds to the penny (a £ sign and thousands separators are fine). Marking: each listed line has two fields (rule, amount); every payout, advance, miles figure and the VAT is a field. Routine fields are worth 1 point; fields that need extra care (shared or uplifted meal limits, approvals and their limits, mileage thresholds and passengers, late or duplicate lines, the £25.00 edge, the VAT) are worth 3, and every payout, advance and miles figure is worth 12 (together about a third of the points). Every line you list that should not be listed costs two fields at 3 points each. Reply with the JSON object only (a ```json code block is fine); key order, spacing and letter case do not matter. cases.notes: [level 10] 6 months, 879 claim lines from 7 employees in 60 claims. Rules in play: 13 families (receipt, hotel, meal, rail, alcohol, late, duplicate, months, entertainment, mileage, conversion, meal-uplift, advances); 376 lines paid less than claimed. Key = audit() of verification/realworld-work/expenses.py over every month's lines in order, exact decimals; second derivations: month-by-month audits over the months so far give every line the same result, the advance set-off step by step equals its closed form, miles summed directly. Trap fields 3 points, routine 1, each payout / advance / miles figure 12. Ladder: ten frozen levels (L01 easiest, L10 hardest), each strictly bigger than the one below and stacking more rule families of the same policy. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.
